content: Diethylpropion is a medication that works by suppressing appetite. It is typically prescribed for short-term use, usually a few weeks, in conjunction with a calorie-restricted diet to aid in weight loss. In some cases, it may be prescribed for other purposes; consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Diethylpropion is available in two forms: regular tablets and extended-release (long-acting) tablets. Regular tablets are usually taken three times a day, one hour before meals. Extended-release tablets are typically taken once daily in the mid-morning. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take diethylpropion exactly as directed. Do not crush, chew, or cut extended-release tablets; swallow them whole. This medication has the potential to be habit-forming. Do not take a larger dose, take it more frequently, or use it for a longer duration than prescribed by your doctor. If you notice that the medication is no longer effective, contact your doctor. Before starting diethylpropion, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to diethylpropion, amphetamines, other diet pills, medications for allergies or colds, or any other drugs. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, herbal products, and vitamins you are taking, especially guanethidine, insulin, and monoamine oxidase (MAO) inhibitors (even if you stopped taking them within the last two weeks). Let your doctor know if you have used other diet pills in the past year. Additionally, inform your doctor if you have or have ever had heart or blood vessel disease, high blood pressure, an overactive thyroid gland, diabetes, glaucoma, pulmonary hypertension, seizures, or a history of drug abuse. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, notify your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking diethylpropion, contact your doctor immediately. If you are scheduled for surgery, including dental surgery, inform your doctor or dentist that you are taking this medication. Be aware that diethylpropion may cause drowsiness. Avoid driving or operating machinery until you know how this medication affects you. Alcohol can exacerbate the drowsiness caused by this drug, so use caution. Follow your doctor’s dietary instructions while taking diethylpropion. Maintain a low-calorie, well-balanced diet. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to make up for a missed one. Diethylpropion may cause side effects. Notify your doctor if you experience any of the following symptoms and they are severe or persistent: dry mouth, unpleasant taste, restlessness, anxiety, dizziness, depression, tremors, upset stomach, vomiting, or increased urination. If you experience any of the following severe side effects, contact your doctor immediately: fast or irregular heartbeat, heart palpitations, blurred vision, skin rash, itching, difficulty breathing, chest pain, fainting, swelling of the ankles or feet, fever, sore throat, chills, or painful urination. If you experience a serious side effect, you or your doctor may report it to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store diethylpropion in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (do not store it in the bathroom). Dispose of any expired or no longer needed medication properly. Consult your pharmacist for guidance on proper disposal. In case of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call 911 immediately. Keep all appointments with your doctor. Your doctor may order tests to monitor your response to diethylpropion. This medication may affect blood sugar levels in diabetic patients and may mask some symptoms of hypoglycemia (low blood sugar). If you notice changes in your urine or blood sugar test results, consult your doctor. Do not share this medication with anyone else. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, ask your pharmacist.
